Air Pollutants
The hundreds of substances in the ambient air which result from man's use of his environment are called air pollutants. Primary pollutants such as carbon monoxide (CO), hydrocarbons (HC), nitrogen oxides (NO), sulfur oxides (SO), particulates (TSP) and lead (Pb), are identified as pollutants which are emitted directly from their respective sources (mobile and stationary). Secondary pollutants are formed by the combination of the primary pollutants in the atmosphere. The most important of these are photochemical oxidants, substances which occur in the ambient air through complicated reactions of nitrogen oxides and oxygen in the presence of sunlight and hydrocarbons. Ozone 
(O_3)
 is the principal oxidant in California air, although nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is the oxidant that gives smog its characteristic brownish color.
Ambient Air Quality Standards
Both federal and state ambient air quality standards have been established to afford protection to the public welfare. The most stringent of these standards are presented in below Programs and sponsoring agencies to achieve the ambient air quality standards are diverse. The major environmental agency at the national level is the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), and at the state level is the California Air Resources Board (CARB). The local air quality authority is the Bay Area Air Pollution Control District (BAAPCD), which conducts air quality monitoring and has authority over the entire San Francisco Bay Area Air Basin. Because of its air quality problems, the San Francisco Bay Area Air Basin has been designated an Air Quality Maintenance Area (AQMA), in accordance with national guidelines. The air basin is mandated by the state to complete an Air Quality Maintenance Plan (AQMP) by the end of 1978, a task which will be taken over by the state if not completed by then. An Environmental Management Task Force, consisting of 46 Bay Area government and nongovernment members, has recently completed recommendations for a draft plan for air quality maintenance and other environmental issues.
